notes: GR10 obliges the MCS to recognize ESI, EMI and EGI and 'establish whatever is necessary to maintain segment, message, or group control'; how is the MCS's. The refuter's subsumption reading (a lone EGI after an EMI marks the already-ended message as ending the group) is not one the text supports and is not implementable in general: once EMI ends a message it is released whole and may be transmitted or received (GR6), and my probe m-emi-then-egi receives HEL (end key 2) BEFORE the lone EGI is sent, so the EGI can no longer be attached to it and must reach the receiver in a unit of its own. GR9 says that without identifier-1 'only the indicator is transmitted', and GR11's 'need not be preceded' makes a preceding EMI optional, not equivalent. The compiler carries a lone indicator as an empty portion with that indicator: EMI then EGI gives HEL (end key 2) and an empty message with end key 3; ESI then EMI gives segment HEL (1) and an empty segment ending the message (2); EGI alone with text gives one message, end key 3. That is a conforming way to 'maintain group control'. The mechanism is the implementor's and is not yet documented. Implementor choice: What does an indicator sent with no identifier-1 (SEND cd WITH EMI/EGI/ESI, or identifier-2 of 1-3) do when nothing is pending? Decided by the implementor, under §1985:XIV.3.6.4 GR10 ('establish whatever is necessary to maintain segment, message, or group control'); GnuCOBOL 3.2 does not implement the module (probe g1), IBM Enterprise COBOL provides none, Micro Focus not checked; documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.3.

next.reason: 1985: "The WITH EGI phrase indicates to the MCS that the group of messages is complete."; 2023: "2023 SEND (14.9.38) is a message-server statement with no WITH EGI/EMI/ESI phrases; the 1985 communication module is dropped". The 2023 SEND sends a message to a message server run unit and has no group, message or segment end indicators. The 1985 EGI/EMI/ESI semantics are not carried.
